description: You are a biomedical engineer at University Hospital preparing to deploy OpenICE's closed-loop drug infusion safety system in the cardiac ICU. The safety system requires two device types working together: a physiological monitoring device that provides continuous SpO2 readings (the safety trigger signal), and a controllable infusion pump device (the device that will be stopped if the patient's SpO2 drops too low). Your tasks: (1) Identify and create the appropriate simulated device adapters for both roles — the physiological monitor and the infusion pump. (2) Launch the clinical application designed for medication infusion safety monitoring and configure the SpO2-based safety interlock threshold — the SpO2 level below which the system should automatically pause drug infusion to protect the patient. (3) Verify that both devices are communicating with the safety application and that the interlock configuration is active. (4) Write a technical configuration report to /home/ga/Desktop/infusion_safety_config.txt documenting: the specific device types you created for each role, the SpO2 threshold value you configured for the safety interlock, and a description of the expected system behavior when a patient's SpO2 drops below that threshold. OpenICE Supervisor is already running on the desktop.

metadata.clinical_context: Closed-loop medication safety interlock for ICU
